title: Calibrated Derivative-Process Sensitivity for Gaussian-Process Variable Selection
summary: Automatic relevance determination (ARD), the default tool for variable selection in Gaussian-process (GP) regression, ranks inputs by inverse lengthscales -- which measure how fast a function varies, not how much an input contributes to prediction -- and offers no calibrated rule for deciding which inputs to keep. The prediction-centred alternative, the derivative sensitivity $ν_j = \mathbb{E}[(\partial f/\partial x_j)^2]$, is available in closed form from a fitted GP, but turning it into a selection rule is harder than it looks: at a null input the estimator is a degenerate quadratic form,…
